Core Research Software Engineer I - Integrated Genomics Core
San Diego, CA
Full-time
Onsite
Entry Level
$33/hr - $38/hr
Salk Institute for Biological Studies is hiring a Research Software Engineer to support the systems and technology infrastructure serving its Core Facilities. The role combines scientific software development with systems administration, operational support, and collaboration with researchers to build and maintain reliable tools and services.
Biotechnology
Education
Life Science
Healthcare
Non Profit
Genetics
Health Care
H1B Sponsor Likely
Responsibilities
Develop, maintain, and release open-source scientific packages for core research purposes, following professional software engineering practices including version control (Git), code review, testing, type checking, and continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD)
Support and make use of shared high-performance computing resources, including GPU cluster scheduling and containerized job workflows (e.g., Kubernetes-based schedulers, SLURM)
Rapidly prototype, build, and iterate on internal applications, command-line tools, and utilities in response to evolving scientific needs
Integrate systems and services through APIs, authentication, and automation to create seamless workflows for end users
Work directly with biologists and other scientists to understand their experimental goals and translate them into technical solutions
Prepare and maintain documentation, runbooks, and training materials that enable researchers to use the tools and pipelines independently
Contribute to the lab’s open-source software community, including reviewing external contributions and responding to user issues
Participate in project planning and status discussions, and coordinate with other Salk labs, Core facilities, and programs
**Systems Monitoring & Maintenance:** Monitor and maintain core facilities system health and capacity, and ensuring service reliability and uptime
**OS Installation & Patching:** Install and configure operating systems (primarily Linux/*NIX and Windows) on servers, workstations, and other Core Facility devices. Apply patches and updates to maintain security and optimize performance
**Backups & Disaster Recovery****:** Execute backup and restore procedures for Core Facilty data, monitor backup jobs (on-premises and cloud) and remediate failures
**Storage Management:** Monitor Core Facility on premis and cloud storage usage. Address routine storage issues and performance or reliability concerns
**Operational Support:** Respond promptly to operational issues. Document resolution steps and follow-up actions for team knowledge sharing
**Continuous Improvement:** Identify and recommend opportunities to improve system reliability, performance, or efficiency. Contribute to Core Facility projects and initiatives, incorporating automation and innovative practices
**Other Duties:** Perform additional related duties as assigned, such as inventory management, procedure documentation, training new team members, or cross-training in other computational areas
Performs other related duties as assigned by management

Required
Operating Systems: Strong proficiency with Linux server administration (such as Red Hat/CentOS or Ubuntu Linux), including shell scripting and command-line tools
Problem-Solving Skills: Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills to diagnose and resolve system issues efficiently. Capable of methodically isolating root causes in complex environments
Communication and Teamwork: Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with an ability to document processes and explain technical issues to non-technical audiences. A customer-service-oriented attitude is essential for working with researchers and staff. Proven ability to work both independently and collaboratively within a team, managing time effectively across multiple tasks
Full-stack software engineering ability, including proficiency in Python and at least one other language and experience building complete applications spanning back-end logic, front-end interfaces, and data storage
Fluency with modern, AI-assisted software development, including the effective use of AI coding tools and large language models (e.g., Claude Code) to design, build, debug, and ship software rapidly
Demonstrated ability to learn unfamiliar systems and technologies quickly and to stand up working services and pipelines through code, scripting, and automation
Comfort working in Linux/Unix environments with version control (Git), testing, and code review
Preferred
BS degree in computer science, engineering, quantitative science, or a related discipline is preferred for this position
Master's degree or post-baccalaureate certification in a computational or scientific field
Prior internship, research, or work experience in a scientific, laboratory, or academic environment
Full-stack web development experience with modern frameworks (e.g., React, Svelte, Vue, FastAPI, Django)
Experience integrating software with scientific instruments or hardware, such as cameras, scanners, or data-acquisition devices
Experience with containerization (e.g., Docker) and with scheduling work on GPU resources (e.g., Kubernetes, SLURM); prior high-performance computing or systems-administration experience is welcome but not required
Experience deploying and maintaining self-hosted applications and services, including on cloud platforms (e.g., AWS, GCP)
Experience maintaining an open-source software project, including packaging, releases, and responding to community issues
Academic coursework, research experience, or demonstrated interest in plant science, biology, neuroscience, or another life-science domain
A track record of shipping small tools or projects quickly and independently, and of picking up new languages, frameworks, and systems with minimal ramp-up
Strong communication skills and the ability to work directly with scientists to translate their needs into technical solutions
A public code portfolio (e.g., GitHub) that demonstrates initiative beyond coursework, such as personal projects or contributions to open-source software
